pulse.currentFocus: Session 337 ran the arc under founder authorization for a full production deploy and found, first, that the deploy had never been identity-blocked: check-promotion-scope returns promotable=true scoped-disjoint and the gate returns allowed=true mode=scoped, and has since S319 — three surfaces had been asserting a blocker the gate itself disagreed with. The dispatched deploy then failed the release ceremony 9/10 on staging-browser-receipt with reason flaky-1, and the cause was ours but not the site's: tests/staging-release.spec.js classifies Trusted Types Report-Only console notices as observations by design, but recognised only Chromium's phrasing. Firefox words the same notice completely differently, so every Firefox report-only notice became a hard console error; the sinks render asynchronously, so it fired on some runs and not others, which Playwright calls flaky, and a flaky result rejects the ceremony. Fixed conjunctively — a report-only marker AND a Trusted Types marker — so an ENFORCED violation still fails loudly, extracted to a shared module, and pinned by a regression spec carrying each engine's verbatim string; proven by 6/6 staging release tests passing locally on all three engines with zero flake. While there, measured the real enforce blocker across 137 built pages: 31 sink-bearing client assets load BEFORE ambient-core installs the Trusted Types default policy they depend on, led by pwa-nav.js on 81 pages and pwa-install.js on 72. Recorded with its numbers and deliberately not fixed — the repair rewrites every page head and invalidates every hash-bound receipt at once. Also closed two Desk truth defects: fact extraction scored register but never subject, so a syndicated promo block published as a sourced fact under a real publisher URL; and no published story recorded which model wrote it while the preferred model is depooled.
pulse.nextMilestone: Hoist the Trusted Types default-policy installer ahead of the 31 client assets that currently load before it, then re-measure and decide the founder-approved enforce flip on real evidence. Then the founder privacy decision on the four silent-zero tables and its one migration, the manual CANON-053 rendered-pixel review of the newly-served surfaces, and a staging parity probe — staging currently serves a route production serves, as a 404.
blockers: TRUSTED TYPES ENFORCE: blocked by a named defect, not only by stale evidence. ambient-core.bundle.js installs the TT default policy that the site's ~167 legacy innerHTML sinks depend on, and its own comment says it MUST load before any sink usage — but it is not the first script on the page. Measured across 137 built pages in S337: 31 sink-bearing assets load before it (pwa-nav.js 81 pages, pwa-install.js 72). Report-Only hides this; enforcement throws. The repair rewrites every page head and invalidates every hash-bound receipt, so it is a session of its own (D-S337.3).

identity/auth surfaces remain held on real-provider-e2e-pending (obelisk.identity.verify missing OBELISK_RP_ID/RP_NAME/RP_ORIGIN; obelisk-staging-registration missing). NOTE (S337, D-S337.1): this holds the IDENTITY BLAST RADIUS only — auth/**, surface:identity, worker:identity. It does NOT block a full production deploy: the S319 scoped path returns allowed=true mode=scoped for any candidate disjoint from that radius, and did so this session.

STAGING PARITY: https://website.staging.vaultsparkstudios.com/how-we-build/ returns 404 while the apex returns 200 — staging is behind production, which inverts the CANON-007 gate the release ceremony depends on. Established by live probe in S337; not yet diagnosed.

PRIVACY DECISION (founder): four public tables — challenge_submissions, game_sessions, point_events, member_achievements — have no anonymous read path, so /community/, all seven /leaderboards/* and public member profiles render zeros and empty states to signed-out visitors. The fix generalizes the S335 public_leaderboard pattern, but it decides which member activity becomes publicly readable and is escalated rather than applied (D-S336.5).

identity: the provider chain is live and verified; production promotion is held only on the real-provider journey, whose remaining leg is a founder passkey ceremony — hardware-key enrollment is founder-reserved by CANON-019 and is deliberately not automatable.

Trusted Types enforcement stays held. Founder approved the flip in S335, but api/tt-readiness.json now honestly reports stale-evidence: its soak manifest is 57 days old against a declared 30-day window. The ageing defect is fixed; the missing input is a fresh KV soak, not a code change.
rollback architecture: the GitHub Pages warm origin still follows mutable main; D-S303 requires explicit founder authorization before migrating to an immutable verified generation.
IGNIS freshness: stale in a studio-ops portfolio artifact this repo cannot write; resolve upstream rather than backdating.
The Dispatch has zero confirmed subscribers until the founder clicks the double-opt-in confirmation email.

startup-revenue-agreement is red: the promoted v5 startup brief renders a revenue evidence age the shared resolver disagrees with, and context/SIGNALS.md is stale. Studio-ops brief-renderer owned; must not be fixed by editing the sibling repo.
